messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT: High error rate detected on serv-runtime-prod (GPU pool). Error class: CUDA illegal memory access / misaligned address. PagerDuty: PD-8241. Auto-escalation -> incidents channel.

alex: acked. I'm on-call. pulling logs now. paging @priya and @jamal.

priya: on my way. any clue if this is a single node or widespread?

alex: initial grep shows repeated stacktraces across several containers:
```
2026-03-12T14:07:02.112Z ERROR runtime: kernel launch failure -> CUDA ERROR: an illegal memory access was encountered
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what():  CUDA illegal memory access
*** Aborted at 1710501222 (unix time) ***
#0 0x7f9d3ac in ...
#5 0x55a3a8d in service::serve_request(...)
```
Also some lines with "misaligned address 0x7f8b3f00" before the crash.

jamal: saw the same on node gpu-rt-12 and gpu-rt-14. Containers are Restarting (OOM?) loop, kube shows Killed SIGSEGV. Node kernel logs have a few GPU driver warnings.

lee: quick check: was there a deploy ~30-40m ago? deploy-bot: `runtime:v2.4.1` -> 2026-03-12T13:33 UTC.

priya: yep that rollout included a low-level attention kernel change + new CUDA kernel parameters. could be a race or misalignment with certain GPUs (A100 vs A10G differences).

alex: mitigation plan (initial):
1) divert traffic off affected nodes/pools -> set routing to fallback smaller model (quantized) to reduce memory pressure
2) cordon & drain suspicious nodes (gpu-rt-12, gpu-rt-14)
3) scale up warm capacity in unaffected pool (dedicated-alt) for throughput
4) if crashes persist on other nodes, rollback runtime -> redeploy previous image v2.4.0
5) inform CS + update status page

priya: +1. I'll run the routing change. alex, can you cordon the nodes? jamal, watch logs for new crashes.

alex: cordoning gpus:```
kubectl cordon gpu-rt-12 && kubectl drain gpu-rt-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl cordon gpu-rt-14 && kubectl drain gpu-rt-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
Nodes drained, pods rescheduled to other pools.

priya: routing change executed: POST https://internal-router/api/v1/routes/serv-runtime set policy -> fallback:quant8 (rollout 100% over 30s). Response 202.

infra-bot: Metric snapshot after diversion: request-rate stable, tail-latency +12%. Error-rate for serv-runtime-prod reduced from 18% -> 4% over 2min.

jamal: still seeing sporadic illegal memory access traces on newly scheduled pods on gpu-rt-03. attaching a local log snippet: 
```
[14:12:38] FATAL: cuda: misaligned address 0x7ffb12a4 (kernel=matmul_attn.cu:212)
[14:12:38] RuntimeError: CUDA illegal memory access
stack: /opt/runtime/serv/core +0x1f3b4
```

alex: hm. that suggests the issue isn't confined to two nodes. Could be kernel-level (device driver) or a race in the new attention kernel that manifests under certain sequences.

priya: I'm going to revert traffic to hosted fallback while we roll back the runtime image. Rolling back to runtime:v2.4.0 now.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated -> runtime:v2.4.0 (image digest sha256:... ). Canary 10% -> 100% over 3min.

infra-bot: Observability note: GPU memory allocs peaked during requests with longer context (seq>2048). Batching config might push large KV cache. Might be exposing misaligned loads in the kernel.

cs-team: heads-up: CS notified top 7 customers flagged as "degraded". We're sending targeted messages to customers with >5 RPS.

alex: after rollback completes we'll watch for recurrence. If rollback clears errors, root cause likely in v2.4.1 kernel change. If not, may be hardware/driver.

(5m later)

deploy-bot: rollback complete -> runtime:v2.4.0 active. Canary success.

infra-bot: error-rate dropped to baseline (0.8%) within 3min of rollback. No new CUDA illegal memory access logs observed on freshly scheduled pods.

jamal: confirming: gpu-rt-03 logs now clean since new pods started under v2.4.0. Previous crash stacks not appearing.

priya: good. I'm going to uncordon nodes after manual inspection. alex, please collect artifacts from crashed pods (core dumps, gpu driver logs) before allowing them back.

alex: grabbing artifacts now. commands: 
```
kubectl -n serv logs <pod> --previous > /tmp/pod-prev.log
kubectl -n serv exec <pod> -- tar czf /tmp/dump.tgz /var/crash /var/log/nvidia* /proc/driver/nvidia
gsutil cp /tmp/dump.tgz gs://redwood-incidents/PD-8241/artifacts/
```
Collected core + driver logs from gpus: gpu-rt-12, gpu-rt-14, gpu-rt-03. Uploaded to bucket PD-8241.

lee: quick kernel/drivers check: driver version nvidia 525.78.01 on all nodes. No kernel patch in last 24h at OS level. That points to runtime change.

priya: assigning followups: 
- runtime-team (priya) -> roll forward a reduced test that isolates attention kernel and fuzz tests on A100 + A10G (due EOD).
- infra (lee) -> ensure node labels and hardware telemetry captured for every crash (due EOD).
- eng-sre (alex/jamal) -> create postmortem draft, include mitigation timeline and artifact links (due tomorrow).

alex: escalation: PD-8241 -> SEV2 -> impact was degraded serving for ~18 minutes before rollback. Customer impact: short latencies increased, failures for some long-context requests. CS sent targeted notes, status page updated to "degraded" then to "operational" after rollback.

priya: I'll open a PR to revert the attention kernel change and add alignment checks in device code. Also triggering extended CI with heavy long-context batching.

jamal: left a note in the cluster events: "containers OOM/SIGSEGV likely due to kernel misalignment after runtime:v2.4.1; rollback to v2.4.0 fixed".

alex: handing over to priya for next steps. I'm stepping off shift in 10m. priya, I'm leaving artifacts + list of affected pods in PD ticket. If anything flares up, ping me on pager.

priya: taking over. summary in PD: rollback -> mitigated; root cause suspected attention kernel misalignment/race in v2.4.1. Next: reproduce, add tests, revert change, and postmortem.

cs-team: we'll follow up with customers to confirm no residual data loss and offer extended monitoring.

infra-bot: closing note: no hardware replacement action required at this time. node health OK.

priya: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. preparing postmortem template. tagging runtime-team for root cause analysis.

alex: thanks everyone. good blameless work. :thumbsup:

(priya later): postmortem draft started at https://docs.internal/redwood/incidents/PD-8241 - will include stack traces, diffs between v2.4.1 and v2.4.0, and test plan.

End of thread."
